newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Kabila says resistance at Lubumbashi.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kabila says resistance at Lubumbashi.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Tuesday his troops were meeting "stiff resistance" in their fight for Lubumbashi from members of President Mobutu Sese Seko's elite guard.
"We are meeting stiff resistance in Lubumbashi but it is something we expected," Kabila told reporters.

"They will be defeated, these DSP (Special Presidential Division) soldiers, there is no doubt about it. Kipushi has been taken and we are moving in many columns so they don't know what is coming after the first salvo," Kabila said.
Rebel forces who took Mbuji-Mayi the diamond capital at the weekend have been advancing for weeks on Lubumbashi, the second largest city and capital of southeast Shaba province.

Mobutu's army has virtually collapsed in the face of the advance by Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire (AFDL) troops who have swept across the eastern half of the vast country in less than six months.
The rebels are conducting peace talks with government representatives in South Africa as well as fighting to oust Mobutu, president since 1965 but now ailing with cancer.
The government delegation at the talks wanted an immediate ceasefire followed by intervention by a multi-national force to act as a buffer between the two sides, Kabila said.
Rapid territorial gains have given rebels a commanding position at negotiations, enabling them to maintain an inflexible bargaining position.
"We are saying he (Mobutu) must negotiate his way out of power, so there is still an open door to discuss...(After that) he will be given a safe haven within the country," Kabila said.
Alliance officials have been predicting the immiment collapse of Lubumbashi for over a week and this is the first time they have acknowledged serious fighting for the city.
The fall of the city should send a strong signal to the government to surrender, deprived of the two cities that produce most of its wealth.
"People should acknowledge that the Alliance has taken the country because there is nothing left in Kinshasa once they are cut off from mining and other riches," Kabila said.
Alliance troops were "present" in Mbandaka province and Bandundu region, he said adding the places were yet to fall.
Mbandaka town is 650 km (406 miles) northeast of the capital Kinshasa on the Zaire river and Bandundu is 300 km (187 miles) northeast of Kinshasa. There was no independent confirmation of the claim.
Government troops deserted Lisala last week, a town on the Zaire river west of third city Kisangani and 220 km (137 miles) south of Mobutu's palace at Gbadolite.
Zairean army units were also fleeing with members of the former Rwandan government army past Kananga 100 km (60 miles) west of Mbuji-Mayi, though the town was not yet taken by rebels.

Kabila earlier attempted to woo a crowd of around 35,000 in Mbuji-Mayi, stronghold of Etienne Tshisekedi, prime minister and veteran opposition leader, with a speech promoting a united front against Mobutu.
